description: Trigger discrimination for database backup verification (D71): proving that real backups exist, are current and restore, versus writing the data-move runbook that needs the backup (data-migration-runbook-author), scheduling periodic audit evidence (compliance-evidence-collector), writing release rollback steps (rollback-runbook-author), personal-data retention in backups (pii-lifecycle-designer), service level objectives (slo-reliability-architect), recurring gated-operation templates (gated-deployment-prompt-template) and live production recovery (incident-response-runbook). The seam with the planned resilience-architecture-reviewer (recovery objectives and disaster-recovery design) is pinned when that skill is on disk, because a routing case may only name skills that exist.

cases.prompt: Explicitly invoke database-backup-verifier. Our recovery point objective is 15 minutes. Check whether the point-in-time recovery window on the orders database is actually keeping up, and whether we have a copy in another account.
cases.reason: Checking real backups against an objective that already exists is verification; setting reliability targets or reviewing the recovery design is not.

cases.prompt: Explicitly invoke database-backup-verifier. Before Saturday's tenant re-shard, prove the customers database backup restores: drill it into a new sandbox instance and measure how long it takes.
cases.reason: Producing the verified-backup evidence is this skill's job; the runbook author consumes that evidence as a precondition.

cases.prompt: Explicitly invoke database-backup-verifier. The auditors want proof of a backup restore test this quarter. Run one on the billing database into a scratch instance and give me the record.
cases.reason: Running the restore drill and recording its result is this skill; the evidence collector schedules and files evidence but never runs a restore.

cases.prompt: Explicitly invoke database-backup-verifier. Our rollback runbook says 'restore from the pre-release snapshot'. Check that snapshot actually exists, is non-empty and is encrypted.
cases.reason: Verifying that the restore point the runbook relies on is real is evidence work; writing the rollback steps is the runbook author's.

cases.prompt: Write the operator runbook for moving tenant data from the old cluster to the new one, with batching, verification queries and abort criteria.
cases.reason: Authoring the data-move runbook belongs to data-migration-runbook-author; this skill only supplies the backup evidence its preconditions require.

cases.prompt: Build our SOC 2 evidence calendar: which artifacts we collect for backups, access reviews and change management, how often, and who owns each.
cases.reason: Scheduling recurring compliance evidence is the collector's job; this skill produces one backup verification when explicitly invoked.

cases.prompt: Write the rollback plan for tomorrow's release: when we roll back versus fix forward, the steps per layer and who decides.
cases.reason: Rollback strategy and steps belong to rollback-runbook-author; this skill never writes rollback steps.

cases.prompt: How long may we keep customer personal data in our database backups, and how does a deletion request reach data that is already in a backup?
cases.reason: Designing retention and deletion rules for personal data in backups is pii-lifecycle-designer's; this skill only checks retention against a requirement that already exists.

cases.prompt: Set availability targets and error budgets for our checkout service, and decide which burn rates should page someone.
cases.reason: Service level objectives and paging belong to slo-reliability-architect; backup verification neither sets targets nor alerts.

cases.prompt: Write the reusable operator prompt template for our monthly production backfills, with a verified-backup gate before each run and a per-run report.
cases.reason: A reusable template for a recurring gated operation is the template author's; this skill produces the backup evidence one run of that gate needs.

cases.prompt: The production orders database is corrupted and checkout is down. Who does what right now, and how do we get service back?
cases.reason: Recovering production during an outage is an incident; this skill never restores into production and only verifies backups outside an incident.
